'''Mango chutney''' is a specialty [[Cookbook:Chutney|chutney]] of the South Indian coastal state of Andhra Pradesh. Mango chutney can be made in many different ways and can be served with poppadoms or with the main course.

== Ingredients ==
* 6 firm under-ripe [[Cookbook:mango|mangoes]], [[Cookbook:Cube|cubed]]
*75 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:raisin|raisins]]
*250 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]) [[Cookbook:cider vinegar|cider vinegar]]
*200 g (1 cup) packed light [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
*2 [[Cookbook:tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*1 ea. (½ cup) finely-chopped medium [[Cookbook:onion|onion]]
*1½ tbsp fresh [[Cookbook:ginger|ginger]], scraped and [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
*2 [[Cookbook:teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]
*¼ tsp [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne pepper]]
*¼ tsp freshly ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]

== Procedure ==
# Dissolve the sugar and salt in the vinegar and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] for 15 minutes.
# Add mangoes, raisins, and onion and bring to the boil again.
# Reduce the heat to low, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 15 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent sticking.
# Add the garlic, ginger and seasoning and simmer for 5 minutes.
# Remove from heat and allow to cool before serving.
# Due to the high sugar and acid content, this chutney may be refrigerated safely for 6 months.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Serve with hot rice or bread.
* This chutney works as an excellent spread on a sandwich.
* If it is not too spicy, you can serve it as a dip for tortilla chips.
* You could also serve with [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yoghurt]]/curd.
* This chutney is typically presented in restaurants in a steel dish with a spoon for serving oneself.
* Vary amount of salt/spices as needed.
